sampling_model.design: Full-support randomized assignment \(Z\in2^{\{A,B,C\}}\) with known or consistently estimated arm probabilities \(\pi_z\).
sampling_model.units: The identification model is superpopulation-based; the inference result uses i.i.d. draws \(O_i=(Z_i,D_i,Y_i)\).
sampling_model.treatment: One-sided WARP-rational received bundles satisfy \(D_i=G_i(Z_i)\subseteq Z_i\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every assignment arm has positive probability; Wald inference additionally requires \(p^\star\ge\kappa>0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate the 27 feasible receipt probabilities and 27 corresponding outcome moments by within-arm sample means, then apply the fixed Möbius and Walsh maps.

body.tldr: A randomized three-factor offer design can tolerate economically meaningful interactive compliance without restricting outcome heterogeneity. The proposed kernel characterizes the unique largest WARP-rational response support containing every coordinate-separable response map for which all eight perfect-complier potential-outcome means remain identified. The class is the union of the perfect-complier map and the WARP maps with zero Boolean Möbius signatures; a symbolic choice argument must show that it contains exactly 29 maps, including 21 interactive maps and six maps for which every offer coordinate matters. Signed assignment-cell transforms identify the eight means, Walsh transforms identify all seven factorial effects, and an explicit Bernoulli null-space construction proves failure after any excluded rational type is added. Joint influence functions yield simultaneous Wald inference away from a zero perfect-complier share, while Bonferroni--Fieller inversion remains honest about weak denominators.

project_justification.gap: Goff's finite-support criterion characterizes outcome-nonrestrictive identification abstractly and gives a two-factor WARP application, while Blackwell and Pashley identify arbitrary-factor perfect-complier effects by imposing coordinate-specific receipt. Neither accessible result supplies a symbolic three-factor WARP envelope that is simultaneously sufficient and maximal for the entire vector of perfect-complier means.
project_justification.niche: Three factors are the first Boolean lattice on which rational, one-sided uptake admits null-signature maps that are interactive in every assignment coordinate. This creates a sharp behavioral boundary that is invisible in the two-factor result and excluded by coordinate-specific treatment receipt.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the Möbius coefficients from the separable baseline, classifies every WARP map annihilated by those coefficients, proves the identifying formulas, and constructs observationally equivalent Bernoulli laws for every forbidden enlargement. The inference rung propagates the common signed denominator through all eight means and seven Walsh contrasts without claiming uniform adaptation as the denominator vanishes.

body.related_work: Goff's Theorems 1--2 provide the finite-support outcome-nonrestrictive row-space criterion that informs the algebraic endpoint here; the present theorem does not claim to improve that generic criterion. Blackwell and Pashley's perfect-complier construction identifies the same factorial targets under coordinate-specific treatment receipt; Theorem 2 strictly enlarges that behavioral support in the one-sided three-factor model. Heckman and Pinto connect rational discrete choice to binary response matrices, which informs the contraction and incidence-matrix proof strategy but does not impose the proposed simultaneous Möbius-null equations. Navjeevan, Pinto, and Santos give an operator-range and generalized-kappa characterization for latent moments, against which the signed recovery functional can be checked. Kormos, Lieli, and Huber show that coordinated two-factor takeup generally mixes causal interaction and heterogeneity, motivating an exact positive class rather than an unrestricted interpretation. Blackwell and Pashley's later bounds paper shows how weaker factorial receipt assumptions typically move the problem to partial identification. Picchetti supplies a current finite-population inference benchmark under factor-specific uptake, while Kang, Peck, and Keele provide the weak-IV inversion logic adapted in the final inference statement.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The separate supplemental material C to Blackwell and Pashley (2023) was not retrievable through the publisher, author page, indexed web results, Crossref metadata, or the accessible 13-page author PDF. The main article describes that supplement as giving a more complicated weighted interpretation under weaker treatment exclusion and says interactions become less clear; it does not expose a maximal three-factor perfect-complier support theorem. Novelty remains conditional on an external audit confirming that supplement C does not admit the six null maps with \(I(g)=\varnothing\) and state an equivalent 29-map envelope. A second diagnostic is internal: equality of the eight probability transforms alone does not certify \(\mathcal M\subseteq\mathcal E_3\), because mixtures of excluded types can cancel their signatures while type-specific outcome moments do not cancel.
body.honest_scope: The open mathematical content is the non-enumerative equality \(\mathcal N_3=\mathcal F_3\), especially the full-offer-pair branch, and the explicit all-additions converse. The row-space criterion, Boolean inversion identity, signed-ratio estimation, multivariate delta method, Wald ellipsoid, and Fieller inversion are established techniques adapted to the classified support. Replacing \(U\) by any two-element factor set collapses the null envelope to the empty map and the two single-factor separable maps; after adding the perfect map, this recovers Goff's four-type two-factor boundary. The proposal does not cover two-sided receipt, missing assignment arms, arbitrary \(K\), classes that omit separable types, rank-adaptive singular Wald inference, or uniform coverage along sequences with \(p_n^\star\to0\).
